blocks.text: Welcome to the Census DataBeast Drivers Course!

We are glad you made it here! The Census Databeast Drivers Course continues where the Census Basics Course left off. Make sure to complete the Census Basics Course before starting the Census Databeast Drivers Course.
Who is this course for and what are the main goals?
This course is for anyone who will be volunteering for as a Databeast Driver. Both for new and returning volunteers. By the end of this course you should be able to:

items: Explain the essential safety protocols and procedures for the safe operation of the Databeast.
Familiarize yourself with the layout and key locations of the Census Lab, Sampling areas and the Commissary.
Review the OnPlaya Forms utilized for your DataBeast Driving Shift.
Understand and commit to your role as a representative of the department, including its mission and behavioral standards.

blocks.text: Driver Qualifications~

To drive the DataBeast, you must first have approval by Census Leadership. Census drivers are REQUIRED to have a Valid and Current Driver’s License from the US or Home Country for International Burners. Additionally, Drivers MUST:

items: Carry your driver's license at all times while operating the Databeast.
Be an excellent, safe & responsible driver with a good driving record.
Have past experience successfully handling a large box truck.
Have attended a minimum of one prior Burn in Black Rock City.
Complete PrePlaya, this HIVE Driver Course.
Complete OnPlaya, Driver orientation before your first shift.
Be comfortable with Burning Man (BM) radio and procedures
Complete PrePlaya. BM Org-Wide Radio Training Video & Art of Radio Guide

blocks.text: If you need help contact our Coordinator of Volunteer Communications at: censusvolunteercoordinators@burningman.org
Let’s get started.
The following Lessons will provide you with the information you need to prepare for your Driving Shift onboard the DataBeast.

items: Drivers are REQUIRED to have a Valid and Current Driver’s License from the US or Home Country for International Burners while driving in Black Rock City.
Seat Belt use is required by BM.org for passenger & driver.
Headlights must be used after sunset.
Don’t exceed 5 mph while in the city. 10 mph between Greeters and Sampling Point.

blocks.text: MUST BE SOBER & SAFELY drive the Census Transport Vehicle:

items: To and from Gate road with teams of Random Sampler & Traffic Tamer volunteers.
To Random locations on Playa & within the City with Teams of Lab Hosts on Pop-ups
To Random locations of Playa for Volunteer Art Tours

While transporting volunteers, there must be a Sampling Shift Lead or Census Lab Host Volunteer in the cab responsible for navigation and being a spotter for pedestrians, bikes, vehicles, etc. Also during transportation, they will operate the Drivers Radio, to communicate with a Shift Lead onboard the DataBeast riding with the volunteers & to Lighthouse before traveling along Gate Road.

Gate Sampling Shifts: Because the Data Beast moves outside of the flags on Gate Road, Lighthouse must be notified before the vehicle moves into this “off limits” area. The Shift Lead is responsible to ensure radio communications are made to Lighthouse after stopping at Greeters, prior to driving to the Census Sampling Point and before returning to Greeters.
Check OUT & RETURN Keys & Radio, inside the office container. Write a COMMENT if FUEL is low or you have any tire or mechanical issues

blocks.text: From BM.org for Mutant Vechiles
Here is a reminder of some of our core driving policies:.

items: Be Sober: Only operate your vehicle when the driver and operational crew is/are completely sober and not impaired or under the influence of alcohol, marijuana or any other intoxicating controlled substance.
Be Respectful: Treat DMV volunteers, other Burning Man Project team members, and law enforcement personnel respectfully.
Drive Slowly: Keep your speed at 5 mph or slower and reduce speed if creating dust or in hazardous conditions.
Yield to Others: Give pedestrians, bicyclists, and emergency vehicles the right of way.
Stay on Approved Routes: you may cross but avoid driving on: Esplanade, the Promenades at 3:00, 6:00, and 9:00.
DO NOT drive within the Great Circle around The Man (check the provided map for details).
Weather Conditions: Do not drive during whiteouts, rain, on wet playa, or during other hazardous conditions.
Respond to Rangers and Staff: Stop immediately if signaled by a Black Rock Ranger, Burning Man staff, or law enforcement.

blocks.text: Operating the DataBeast

items: Unplug DataBeast from charging cable (labeled Electric cord)
Secure any open windows or doors
Confirm back ladder is stowed in the UP/Closed position
Operate winch to Raise & Lower ladder Winch is operated by 12V battery on top deck. Be sure there is an extra battery if operation slows down
Before heading out, wait until you hear a “Clear to Go” radio call from the Shift Lead Onboard the DataBeast
Shift to Neutral
Insert key
Turn key to right. Wait for lights to stop flashing then crank engine on. Beeping will begin from the instrument panel.
Wait until until air pressure builds. Time varies based on period of inactivity. Beeping will stop when it's warmed up.
Push Yellow button to release air brakes
Shift into drive - 5mph limit

blocks.text: Volunteer Assistance
Shift-Leads are responsible for getting everyone situated on the DataBeast

items: Make sure water container is accessible to volunteers
Assist Volunteers/Participants UP & DOWN the ladder
Assist Shift leads as needed
Assist with managing MOOP

lessons.title: Driving Routes to Commissary & Sampling Point from Census Lab @ 6:30 & A

blocks.text: COMMISSARY: Commissary is located at 5:30 between E & G. The Simplest way to Commissary from Census Lab, is to travel down 6:30 to C, turn left towards 5:30, then turn right at 5:30 until you reach the fenced Commissary area at E, look for the large tented structure. From the Sampling Point, turn right when you get into the City, turn left onto 5:30 travel to E street. Park at 5:30 and E, next to the black partitions.

items: Park at 5:30 and E, next to the black partitions, where space is available.
Close Door & Stairs while volunteers are having their meal.

blocks.text: SAMPLING POINT: From Census Lab, travel down 6:30 towards Gate Road. When you get to the end of the City, turn left towards Greeters. From Commissary, continue on 5:30 to the end of the City, then turn right towards Greeters. Stop at Greeters to let them know you will need to cross into the East side of the fenced line to reach our Sampling Point, then have Shift Lead radio Lighthouse.

items: During sampling runs to and from Gate or Popups, avoid getting talked into detouring to drop-off or pick-up people or missing items. They invariably take more time than it sounds. Let the Shift Leads make the ultimate decisions.

When returning from the shift, it may be okay to let people get out before getting back to the Commissary or Census Lab at end of shift. Make sure you come to a complete stop & lower the ladder before allowing people to get out.
Seat Belt use is required by BM.org for passenger & driver.
Headlights must be used after sunset.
Don’t exceed 5 mph while in the city. 10 mph between Greeters and Sampling Point.
RETURN to Census Lab @ 6:30 & A
Secure in Designated DataBeast Parking at Census Lab
Final MOOP Sweep
Roll Up Windows
Secure Doors & Raise Stairs
Plug DataBeast into charging cable (labeled Electric cord)
Check IN Keys & Radio, inside the office container. REMEMBER to write a COMMENT if FUEL is low or you have any tire or mechanical issues.

sections.title: DataBeast Course Summary and Completion Confirmation

blocks.text: Summary
Thank you for joining the Census DataBeast Driver Course. We're excited to have you on board and appreciate your dedication. Here’s a quick recap of what you’ve learned:

items: Understand Your Role: You now have a clear picture of what your specific role involves at Census.
Explain the essential safety protocols and procedures for the safe operation of the Databeast.
Familiarize yourself with the layout and key locations of the Census Lab, Sampling areas and the Commissary.
Understand the OnPlaya Forms utilized for your DataBeast Driving Shift.
Understand and commit to your role as a representative of the department, including its mission and behavioral standards.

blocks.text: Finally, remember to HAVE FUN! Make friends, be silly, and let your beautiful personality shine through!
What's Next:
Thank you for sticking with us all the way through this course!! Before you leave for Burning Man:

items: If it sounds like fun, find and decorate your own lab coat using Census team colors (hot pink and black). Please don’t use other colors, we want you to be easily identifiable as a Census volunteer!

Update your schedule if your availability changes. You can log into Shiftboard to Call Out or Unassign from a shift up to 5 days before the shift takes place. If your availability changes with less than 5 days’ notice please email censusvolunteercoordinators@burningman.org (if you are not yet on-playa) or stop by Census Lab to remove yourself using the tablet.
Read all emails from Census carefully, as they will have details about your arrival.
QUESTIONS? Contact: censusvolunteercoordinators@burningman.org

blocks.text: Thank you from all of us on the Census Team and we can't wait to see you in the dust!
